article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Indica / 40% Sativa
Genetics: Milk & Cookies × Rainbow Chip
Breeder: Exotic Genetix
THC Content: 23–30%
CBD Content: 1%
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , Limonene , Myrcene
Primary Flavors: Vanilla frosting, sweet cookie dough
Flowering Time (Indoor): 56–63 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to October
Indoor Yield: Medium to Heavy
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to High
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

A baker’s dozen traditionally means thirteen instead of twelve, a small extra reward that makes an ordinary purchase feel more generous. Exotic Genetix carried that idea into cannabis breeding with Baker’s Dozen , a weed strain created to deliver an abundance of the characteristics that made its parent strains desirable. Sweet vanilla, creamy cookie dough, colorful flowers, and thick resin coverage come together in a marijuana hybrid built around two influential genetic families.

By combining Milk & Cookies with Rainbow Chip, the breeder developed a plant that emphasizes dessert-inspired flavors without abandoning the earthy pungency and physical intensity of traditional Kush genetics. Its medium-height structure supports numerous flowering branches, while mature buds can develop impressive layers of crystalline trichomes. Beyond its qualities as finished flower, the cultivar became an important foundation for an extensive breeding collection, establishing its reputation as more than another sweet-smelling weed variety .
Genetics and Lineage

Baker’s Dozen originated from a direct cross between Milk & Cookies and Rainbow Chip, two established creations from Exotic Genetix. The maternal parent, Milk & Cookies, combines Cookies & Cream with Triple OG. Cookies & Cream was developed using Girl Scout Cookies and Starfighter F2, bringing together sweet vanilla characteristics, dense flower development, and the substantial resin production associated with Alien-related genetics. Starfighter traces its background to Lemon Alien Dawg and Tahoe Alien , introducing additional pungency and trichome potential. Triple OG contributes a heavier genetic foundation through Triangle Kush , Constantine, and Master Yoda. These varieties connect Milk & Cookies to classic OG Kush breeding, reinforcing its earthy fragrance, sturdy growth, and physically relaxing characteristics. The resulting parent combines bakery-like sweetness with the deeper aromatic intensity of traditional marijuana.

Rainbow Chip introduces a contrasting combination of fruit, mint, and colorful flower characteristics. Exotic Genetix created this parent by crossing Sunset Sherbet with Mint Chocolate Chip . Sunset Sherbet descends from Girl Scout Cookies and Pink Panties , contributing sweet berry aromas, creamy undertones, and characteristics associated with dense, resinous buds. Mint Chocolate Chip combines SinMint Cookies with Green Ribbon BX genetics, introducing herbal freshness, chocolate-like sweetness, and additional aromatic complexity. The pairing brings several recognizable Cookies-family influences into Baker’s Dozen without making the finished hybrid a simple reproduction of either parent. The breeder originally offered regular seeds using Milk & Cookies as the mother and Rainbow Chip as the father, and later released a feminized version using a reversed Rainbow Chip selection.

Its importance extends into subsequent breeding projects. Exotic Genetix selected Baker’s Dozen as the foundation of the Baker’s Dozen Reloaded collection, producing numerous hybrids with established cultivars including Jealousy , Sherb N’ Sour, and Rainbow Runtz . This continued use reflects the genetic line’s desirable combination of production characteristics, aromatic richness, and resin development.
Effects and Experience

The experience associated with Baker’s Dozen tends to favor a comfortable cerebral beginning followed by increasingly noticeable physical relaxation. Early intoxication may bring a pleasant change in mood, a greater appreciation for music, and heightened interest in familiar surroundings. Rather than producing an intense burst of energy, the mental effects can feel warm and unhurried, making conversation or quiet entertainment especially enjoyable. Some consumers experience mild euphoria or spontaneous laughter, while others notice a reduction in distracting thoughts. The Rainbow Chip influence may contribute to this engaging opening character, although cannabinoid concentrations and individual sensitivity remain more important than lineage when determining the actual effects.

As the experience develops, the heavier Milk & Cookies ancestry may become more apparent. Muscular tension can feel less prominent, physical restlessness may diminish, and comfortable relaxation can gradually turn into pronounced bodily heaviness. Larger amounts may encourage appetite, reduced motivation, or sleepiness, making this hybrid especially appealing for relaxed evenings. Its potentially substantial THC concentrations deserve attention because inexperienced consumers may find the psychoactive effects overwhelming. Excessive consumption can produce dizziness, dry mouth, anxiety, increased heart rate, or impaired concentration. Even when the experience feels mentally clear, cannabis intoxication can affect coordination and judgment. The cultivar should not be consumed before driving or performing safety-sensitive activities.
Medical Benefits

The physically relaxing qualities associated with Baker’s Dozen may interest medical marijuana patients exploring cannabinoid-based approaches to persistent discomfort. THC interacts with the endocannabinoid system, influencing neurological pathways involved in pain perception, appetite, and other physiological processes. Clinical research indicates that certain cannabis preparations may provide modest benefits for selected chronic pain conditions, although results vary considerably. A hybrid that combines initial mental uplift with later physical relaxation may appeal to patients seeking comfort without immediately experiencing heavy sedation. However, no controlled clinical trials have established Baker’s Dozen itself as an effective treatment for chronic pain, muscular tension, or another specific medical condition.

Difficulty unwinding, reduced appetite, and sleep disturbances represent additional reasons some individuals consider indica-dominant cannabis. THC can temporarily stimulate hunger and may produce drowsiness as intoxication progresses. These effects are not universally beneficial, and high doses can worsen anxiety or cause uncomfortable psychological reactions. Frequent consumption of potent weed can contribute to tolerance, dependence, memory impairment, and changes in normal sleep patterns. Patients taking sedatives, psychiatric medications, or other prescription treatments should discuss cannabis use with a qualified healthcare professional. Product-specific laboratory testing and individual medical circumstances remain essential when considering any potential medical application.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The fragrance of Baker’s Dozen is built around the unmistakable richness of sweet bakery ingredients. Fresh flowers may release aromas resembling vanilla frosting, warm cookie dough, and sweet cream, followed by subtle impressions of chocolate and ripe berries. Milk & Cookies provides much of the creamy foundation, while Rainbow Chip introduces softer fruit characteristics and herbal freshness. Beneath the sweetness lies a more traditional cannabis fragrance of earthy resin, woody spice, and occasional fuel-like pungency. Some phenotypes may emphasize vanilla and pastry, while others display stronger berry, mint, or earthy characteristics. Breaking apart mature buds can intensify these contrasting fragrances as aromatic compounds are released from the resinous flower surfaces.

Several terpenes commonly associated with the parental lines may contribute to this aromatic complexity. Beta-caryophyllene produces peppery, woody impressions that complement the heavier Kush-related characteristics. Limonene can introduce citrus brightness, while myrcene contributes earthy and herbal qualities. Linalool, when present, may soften the profile with subtle floral notes. Exact terpene concentrations vary between phenotypes and harvests, and the recognizable vanilla and chocolate impressions cannot be attributed to individual terpenes alone. On the palate, creamy sweetness often takes the lead, followed by cookie dough, mild fruit, and a deeper earthy finish. Well-preserved flower may retain a delicate herbal or mint-like aftertaste that distinguishes it from simpler vanilla-dominant cannabis varieties. Careful curing and storage help maintain these aromatic details by limiting the degradation of volatile compounds.
Growing Information

Baker’s Dozen combines manageable plant height with substantial lateral development, producing the multi-topped bush structure identified by Exotic Genetix. Its medium-sized frame makes it suitable for cultivation environments where exceptionally tall plants are impractical, while sturdy branching supports numerous productive flowering sites. During vegetative growth, healthy specimens may establish broad foliage and relatively strong secondary stems. As flowering begins, the plant directs increasing resources toward compact bud clusters that accumulate substantial glandular trichomes. Rainbow Chip contributes the potential for colorful pigmentation, including purple and darker green expressions, while Milk & Cookies reinforces dense flower structure and resin production. Individual seedlings may display differences in branching, internodal spacing, and final flower appearance.

Indoor flowering generally requires 56–63 days, placing the cultivar within a relatively efficient eight-to-nine-week production window. Exotic Genetix classifies its yield potential as medium to heavy, making productive flowering an important part of its horticultural identity. Maintaining an even canopy can help distribute light across the numerous flowering sites, while selective pruning may improve airflow around crowded branches. As buds develop, additional structural support may become useful where particularly heavy flower clusters form. Dense, resin-rich flowers require careful humidity management because trapped moisture can increase the risk of fungal contamination. Balanced nutrition, stable environmental conditions, and healthy root development support consistent flower maturation without compromising aromatic quality.

Outdoor cultivation is possible in locations with abundant sunlight and relatively dry autumn weather. A late September through October harvest provides a preliminary Northern Hemisphere expectation, although precise outdoor maturity has not been standardized by the breeder. Given adequate space, plants may develop broader branching structures than specimens maintained indoors. Mature flowers can display swollen calyxes, orange pistils, and a thick crystalline coating that makes the buds appear heavily frosted. Some selections develop purple pigmentation, but coloration alone does not indicate potency. After harvest, controlled drying and curing are particularly important for protecting the delicate vanilla, fruit, and herbal aromas. Intermediate cultivation experience is helpful for managing productive branches, protecting dense flowers, and preserving the finished cannabis flower’s resin quality.
FAQ
Is Baker’s Dozen indica or sativa?

Baker’s Dozen is an indica-dominant hybrid classified by Exotic Genetix as approximately 60% indica and 40% sativa. Its parents are Milk & Cookies and Rainbow Chip. The experience generally emphasizes mental euphoria followed by progressively stronger physical relaxation. Individual effects depend on cannabinoid concentration, consumption amount, and personal tolerance.
How much THC does Baker’s Dozen have?

Commercial descriptions frequently associate the cultivar with substantial THC potential, sometimes estimating concentrations around 23–30%. However, the breeder has not established a standardized laboratory-confirmed THC range for every phenotype. Actual potency varies according to cultivation conditions, plant selection, and harvest. CBD content is generally expected to remain low.
What does Baker’s Dozen taste like?

The flavor combines vanilla frosting, sweet cookie dough, creamy chocolate, ripe berries, and subtle herbal mint. Milk & Cookies contributes the rich bakery qualities, while Rainbow Chip introduces fruit sweetness and additional aromatic complexity. Some phenotypes display stronger earthy gas or peppery characteristics beneath the creamy foundation.
How long does Baker’s Dozen take to flower?

Indoor flowering generally requires 56–63 days, equivalent to approximately eight or nine weeks. Exotic Genetix describes medium-height plants with a multi-topped bush structure and medium-to-heavy production potential. Outdoor harvest timing depends on climate and phenotype, with autumn maturity expected under suitable Northern Hemisphere conditions.
Who bred Baker’s Dozen, and what are its parent strains?

Baker’s Dozen was developed by Exotic Genetix using Milk & Cookies as the mother and Rainbow Chip as the pollen parent. Milk & Cookies combines Cookies & Cream with Triple OG, while Rainbow Chip descends from Sunset Sherbet and Mint Chocolate Chip. Both regular and feminized seed releases have been produced. The cultivar also became the foundation of the Baker’s Dozen Reloaded breeding collection.
Final Thoughts on Baker’s Dozen

Baker’s Dozen represents an important achievement within Exotic Genetix’s extensive work with Cookies-related cannabis genetics. By combining Milk & Cookies with Rainbow Chip, the breeder created a marijuana hybrid that concentrates creamy vanilla, bakery sweetness, subtle fruit, and earthy Kush characteristics within a productive, resin-rich plant. Its medium-height structure, multiple flowering tops, and relatively short maturation period give the cultivar practical horticultural appeal, while dense trichome-covered buds reinforce its reputation for premium flower quality.

For experienced cannabis enthusiasts, the most compelling qualities are its rich dessert fragrance and the progression from pleasant cerebral effects toward deeper physical relaxation. Growers may appreciate its productive branching and manageable flowering period, particularly when visual flower quality and aromatic preservation are priorities. Its subsequent use as the central genetic parent of the Baker’s Dozen Reloaded collection demonstrates the lasting value of the original cross. Rather than remaining a single dessert-inspired weed variety, Baker’s Dozen became a foundation for an entire family of modern American cannabis hybrids, preserving the influence of Milk & Cookies and Rainbow Chip across numerous distinctive genetic combinations.
